sn5.7:0.3: The Discourse about Upacālā Thus I have heard:
sn5.7:1.1: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.
sn5.7:1.2: Then the nun Upacālā, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up her bowl and robe, was entering Sāvatthī for alms. After walking for alms in Sāvatthī, and returning from the alms-round after the meal, she approached the Blind Man’s Wood to pass the day, and having entered Blind Man’s Wood,
sn5.7:1.3: she sat down at the root of a certain tree to pass the day.
sn5.7:1.4: Then the Wicked Māra approached the nun Upacālā, and after approaching he said this to the nun Upacālā:
sn5.7:1.5: “Where would you, nun, like to be reborn?”
sn5.7:1.6: “There is nowhere, friend, I would like to be reborn.”
sn5.7:2.3: Those gods who delight in creation,
sn5.7:2.4: those gods who are Wielding Power,
sn5.7:2.5: To those places direct your mind,
sn5.7:3.3: Those gods who delight in creation,
sn5.7:3.4: those gods who are Wielding Power,
sn5.7:3.5: Those bound by sensual-bondage come to Māra’s power again.
sn5.7:4.1: The whole of the world is in flames,
sn5.7:4.2: the whole of the world is blazing,
sn5.7:4.3: The whole of the world is burning,
sn5.7:4.4: the whole of the world is shaking.
sn5.7:5.4: (for) there my mind does not delight.”
sn5.7:6.1: Then the Wicked Māra (thought): “The nun Upacālā knows me!” and pained and depressed he vanished right there.
